title: Two Formosan Black Bears Spotted Near a Nantou Hiking Trail
summaryZh: 能高越嶺道出現兩隻台灣黑熊，林業署提醒山友注意安全。
summaryHi: नानतोउ की एक पगडंडी के पास दो फ़ॉर्मोसन काले भालू दिखे; पैदल यात्रियों को सावधान रहने की सलाह।
summaryEs: Avistan dos osos negros de Formosa cerca de un sendero de Nantou; piden precaución a los excursionistas.
summaryJa: 南投の能高越嶺道付近でタイワンツキノワグマ2頭を目撃、登山者に注意呼びかけ。
summaryKo: 난터우 넝가오 산길 근처에서 대만흑곰 2마리 목격… 등산객 주의 당부.
summaryEn: Two Formosan black bears were seen near the Nenggao Cross-Ridge Trail, and officials are asking hikers to take care.
paragraphs: Forestry officials in central Taiwan have issued a safety warning to hikers after two Formosan black bears were seen close to the Nenggao Cross-Ridge Trail in Nantou County.

The Nantou Branch of the Forestry and Nature Conservation Agency said the bears were spotted on Monday afternoon near the 3.3 to 3.4 kilometre section of the trail. The hikers who saw them captured the encounter on video and reported it on Tuesday.

The Formosan black bear is Taiwan's only native bear species and is legally protected. In response to the sighting, the agency said it was monitoring bear activity, raising public awareness and reminding visitors to store food and rubbish properly, since leftovers can draw bears towards people.
Hikers have been advised not to walk alone and to carry bear bells, bear spray or other devices that make noise, which can warn bears of their presence.

Anyone who comes across a bear should remain calm, keep a safe distance and avoid approaching or photographing it. Sightings can be reported via the hotline 0800-000-930 or through the agency's online Human-Animal Coexistence Management Reporting Platform.
Hikers in Nantou County, in central Taiwan, saw two Formosan black bears on Monday, 9 November. The bears were near the Nenggao Cross-Ridge Trail, a popular mountain path.
The hikers made a video of the bears. They were about 3.3 to 3.4 kilometres along the trail. The hikers told the forestry office on Tuesday.
The Formosan black bear is a special animal in Taiwan. There are not many of them, and the law protects them.
The forestry office now asks hikers to be careful. Do not walk alone. Take a bear bell or something that makes noise. Keep your food and rubbish in a safe place.
If you see a bear, stay calm. Do not go near it, and do not take photos of it. Keep a safe distance and call the hotline 0800-000-930.

paragraphs: Forest officials in central Taiwan have asked hikers to be careful after two Formosan black bears were seen near the Nenggao Cross-Ridge Trail in Nantou County.

According to the Nantou Branch of the Forestry and Nature Conservation Agency, hikers spotted the two bears on Monday afternoon between the 3.3 km and 3.4 km points of the trail. They filmed the animals and reported the sighting the next day.
The Formosan black bear is Taiwan's only native bear and a protected species. After the report, the agency said it would watch bear activity in the area and remind visitors about safety.

The agency gave hikers several pieces of advice. They should not hike alone, and they should carry bear bells, bear spray or other things that make noise. Food and rubbish must be stored properly so that bears are not attracted to them.

Anyone who meets a bear should stay calm and keep a safe distance. People should not walk towards the animal or try to take photos. Sightings can be reported on the free hotline 0800-000-930 or through the agency's online reporting platform.

該署給了山友幾項建議。
山友不應獨自健行，並應攜帶熊鈴、防熊噴霧或其他會發出聲音的物品。
食物和垃圾必須妥善存放，才不會引來黑熊。

paragraphs: Conservation authorities in central Taiwan have urged hikers to exercise caution after two Formosan black bears were sighted in the vicinity of the Nenggao Cross-Ridge Trail, a mountain route in Nantou County.

According to the Nantou Branch of the Forestry and Nature Conservation Agency, hikers encountered the pair on Monday afternoon between the 3.3 and 3.4 kilometre markers, filmed them and alerted officials the following day.

The Formosan black bear, the island's sole native bear species, enjoys legal protection. In the wake of the sighting, the agency said it had begun monitoring bear activity and was working to raise public awareness, including reminders that food and refuse must be stored securely.
Its guidance to visitors is unambiguous: avoid hiking alone and carry bear bells, bear spray or other noise-making devices.

Should anyone come face to face with a bear, they are advised to remain composed, maintain a safe distance and resist the temptation to approach or photograph the animal. Encounters can be reported through the hotline 0800-000-930 or the agency's online Human-Animal Coexistence Management Reporting Platform.

據林業及自然保育署南投分署表示，山友週一下午在3.3至3.4公里里程標之間遇見這對黑熊，拍下影像，並於隔天通報官員。
台灣黑熊是本島唯一的原生熊種，受到法律保護。
目擊事件發生後，該署表示已開始監測黑熊活動，並努力提升民眾意識，包括提醒食物和垃圾必須妥善封存。
該署給遊客的指引十分明確：避免獨自健行，並攜帶熊鈴、防熊噴霧或其他能發出聲響的裝置。
萬一與熊正面相遇，民眾應保持鎮定、維持安全距離，並忍住靠近或拍攝動物的衝動。
目擊情況可透過專線0800-000-930或該署的線上「人與動物共存管理通報平台」回報。

paragraphs: Hikers in central Taiwan have been urged to remain vigilant following the sighting of two Formosan black bears near the Nenggao Cross-Ridge Trail in Nantou County, a reminder that the island's mountain trails pass through genuine wildlife habitat.

The Nantou Branch of the Forestry and Nature Conservation Agency reported that the animals were observed on Monday afternoon along the 3.3 to 3.4 kilometre stretch of the route. The hikers who witnessed them recorded footage and notified the authorities on Tuesday.

As Taiwan's only indigenous bear species, the Formosan black bear is protected by law. The agency has responded by monitoring bear movements, promoting public awareness and emphasising the importance of storing food and waste appropriately, as careless disposal can lure wildlife towards humans.
Visitors have also been advised against hiking alone and encouraged to carry bear bells, bear spray or other noise-making equipment.

In the event of an encounter, hikers should stay composed, maintain a safe distance and refrain from approaching or photographing the bear. Sightings may be reported via the hotline 0800-000-930 or the agency's online Human-Animal Coexistence Management Reporting Platform.
sentZh: 南投縣能高越嶺道附近目擊兩隻台灣黑熊後，台灣中部的山友被呼籲保持警覺；這也提醒大家，島上的山徑確實穿越野生動物的棲息地。
林業及自然保育署南投分署表示，這些動物於週一下午在該路線3.3至3.4公里路段被觀察到。
目擊的山友錄下影片，並在週二通報主管機關。
台灣黑熊是台灣唯一的原生熊種，受法律保護。
該署的回應包括監測黑熊動向、推廣民眾意識，並強調妥善存放食物與廢棄物的重要性，因為隨意丟棄可能把野生動物引向人類。
當局也建議遊客不要獨自健行，並鼓勵攜帶熊鈴、防熊噴霧或其他能發出聲響的裝備。
萬一遇到熊，山友應保持鎮定、維持安全距離，並避免靠近或拍攝黑熊。
目擊情況可透過專線0800-000-930或該署的線上「人與動物共存管理通報平台」通報。
